best_for: Linux and Windows users who keep research, code snippets or a personal wiki in one tree of notes and want it all in a single local file.
description:
CherryTree is a hierarchical note-taking app written by Giuseppe Penone (giuspen) and Evgenii Gurianov (txe). Volunteers have translated it into more than 20 languages, from Arabic and Chinese to Turkish and Ukrainian.

Notes can hold bulleted, numbered and to-do lists, and you can link to web pages, other notes, files or folders, or link to a note just by typing its name inside double square brackets. Find and replace work in one note, a branch or the whole tree. Copy and paste works with apps such as LibreOffice and Gmail, and dragging files in from your file manager adds a list of links to them. On Linux and Mac, an embedded terminal sits inside the app.

points.title: One file holds the whole tree
points.text: A notebook saves as one XML or SQLite file, or as a folder of files if you prefer. That makes it easy to back up, copy to a USB stick or sync with any file-sync tool you already use.

points.title: Rich text and code in the same note
points.text: Nodes take formatted text, images, tables, attached files and LaTeX math. Code boxes get syntax highlighting, and some code can be run from inside the app.

points.title: Password protection has a catch
points.text: You can lock a single-file notebook with a password, using 7-Zip. It does not work for the multi-file format, and while the notebook is open an unlocked copy sits in a temp folder until you close the app.

points.title: Moves in from other note apps
points.text: It imports from Tomboy, Zim, Keynote, Notecase and others. Going out, you can export a node, a branch or the whole tree to HTML, plain text or PDF, and tables to CSV.

points.title: Free and GPL licensed
points.text: The source is under GPLv3 or later, and your notes stay in files you control rather than on someone else's server.

points.title: Windows: installer or portable
points.text: The Windows listing here keeps 9 versions of the 64-bit installer, which installs for all users. The project also offers a portable 7z archive that keeps its settings next to the program.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is the developer's own
points.text: The Flathub build is marked verified as published by Giuseppe Penone, for x64 and Arm64. Only the current release is listed for Linux here; the project also offers an AppImage, Snap, .deb and RPM packages.

points.title: Mac is not listed here
points.text: CherryTree does run on macOS, but the project ships it there through an installer, Homebrew or MacPorts rather than the builds this site tracks.
